description: Technical Track B: State Transitions & Optimization Problems

prompts.statement: Given two strings word1 and word2, return the minimum number of operations required to convert word1 to word2. You have the following three operations permitted on a word: insert a character, delete a character, or replace a character.
constraints: word1 and word2 consist of lowercase English letters
Expected O(m * n) time and O(min(m, n)) auxiliary space

examples.explanation: intention -> inention (remove 't') -> enention (replace 'i' with 'e') -> exention (replace 'n' with 'x') -> exection (replace 'n' with 'c') -> execution (insert 'u').

clarificationBranches.question: What if one or both of the strings are empty?
clarificationBranches.answer: If one string is empty, the distance is simply the length of the other string (all insertions or deletions).

followups.question: How can you optimize the auxiliary space from O(m * n) to O(min(m, n))?
followups.criterion: Uses two rolling 1D arrays or a single array with a temporary variable to track the diagonal previous value.

privateReference.approach: 2D dynamic programming where dp[i][j] is the edit distance between word1[0..i-1] and word2[0..j-1]. If word1[i-1] == word2[j-1], dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1]. Otherwise 1 + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1], dp[i-1][j-1]) representing delete, insert, replace.
checks: Correctly minimizes over insertion, deletion, replacement
privateReference.expectedComplexity: O(m * n) time, O(min(m, n)) space
